extracted.intended_audience: product managers and founders doing PR (especially for product launches and startups)
extracted.subtask_description: Practical checklist and playbook for product managers and founders deciding when to do PR, how to write a launch press release and quotes, how to distribute, and which metrics to track.

rubrics_metrics.name: Major product launch
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as a situation when PR is actually worth doing; explicitly excludes minor releases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding announcement
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only worth PR if Series A+. Use PR selectively for funding rounds that materially change perception or resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: New executive hire
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only if name-brand — don't announce routine hires.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industry-shifting data report
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use PR for reports or data that materially change industry conversations or benchmarks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Crisis or controversy response
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PR is appropriate when responding to incidents that require public explanation or reputation management.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minor feature ships (don't do PR)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed under 'When NOT to Do PR' — avoid press for small product tweaks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hiring junior team members (don't do PR)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid PR for routine hiring that does not change external perception.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vanity awards (don't do PR)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Don't pursue or announce low-quality awards purely for marketing optics.

rubrics_metrics.name: "Thought leadership" with no actual point (don't do PR)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid PR around vague thought pieces that don't offer a concrete insight or news hook.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anything you'd be embarrassed by in 6 months (don't do PR)
rubrics_metrics.description: Anything you'd be embarrassed by in 6 months
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a story will look foolish or transient on a short timeline, don't PR it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hook (Product Launch Release Formula)
rubrics_metrics.description: Hook: What's now possible that wasn't before
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lead with the new capability or change in possibility; the hook should explain the direct, novel value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mechanism (Product Launch Release Formula)
rubrics_metrics.description: Mechanism: How does the product actually work
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain the concrete mechanism or technical approach that enables the hook—avoid vague marketing-speak.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proof (Product Launch Release Formula)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proof: Beta customer logo or quote
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include real proof points such as customer logos, quotes, or measurable early results to substantiate claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stakes (Product Launch Release Formula)
rubrics_metrics.description: Stakes: Why this matters to the industry
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain the broader implications and why audience or industry should care.

rubrics_metrics.name: Action (Product Launch Release Formula)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give a clear next step (trial link, signup, demo) so interested readers can act immediately.

rubrics_metrics.name: "We're excited to announce..." (quote anti-pattern)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid clichéd, generic opening quote lines that add no specificity or human detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: "Today marks a milestone..." (quote anti-pattern)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid generic milestone language that reads like boilerplate PR copy.

rubrics_metrics.name: "Our mission has always been..." (quote anti-pattern)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid mission-statement fluff in quotes; it doesn't make quotes feel human or newsworthy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quotes that contain marketing taglines (anti-pattern)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Don't use quotes that are just marketing lines—quotes should add human perspective or insight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quotes attributed to executives who didn't say them (anti-pattern)
rubrics_metrics.description: Quotes attributed to executives who didn't say them
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid fabricating or recycling quotes; attribution must be authentic and attributable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific user complaint that drove the work (quote pattern)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific user complaint that drove the work
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Good quotes often call out a concrete user problem that motivated the product decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Counter-intuitive design decision and why (quote pattern)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quotes that explain surprising tradeoffs or design choices create interesting human insight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hard tradeoff the team wrestled with (quote pattern)
rubrics_metrics.description: Hard tradeoff the team wrestled with
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Honest discussion of tradeoffs makes quotes feel real and informative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Surprising number from internal data (quote pattern)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A specific, unexpected data point can be an effective quote element—use concrete numbers when possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Honest admission of what's still unsolved (quote pattern)
rubrics_metrics.description: Honest admission of what's still unsolved
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Admitting limitations or open problems in a quote increases credibility and humanizes the team.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distribution order
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prescribed sequence for distributing a release: 1) Embargoed exclusive to top trade publication; 2) Hours later: pitch to 5–10 secondary outlets; 3) Then wire release for SEO; 4) Then post on company newsroom; 5) Then social and community channels. Follow embargo-first for top-tier exclusives, then broaden distribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality of coverage > quantity (metric)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure the quality and relevance of placements rather than raw number of hits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inbound from VCs, partners, customers (metric)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track meaningful inbound interest from investors, potential partners, and customers as a result of coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hiring pipeline lift (metric)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure whether PR improves candidate volume/quality for hiring needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sales lead lift in 30 days (metric)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track short-term sales or lead generation attributable to the PR campaign within a 30-day window.

rubrics_metrics.name: Long-tail SEO from earned coverage (metric)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider the ongoing organic traffic and discoverability benefits of earned media over time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Worth-doing test passed (implicit quality rubric)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implicit criterion: ensure the story is real news and passes the 'worth doing' filter before investing in PR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hook describes new possibility (implicit quality rubric)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implicit requirement: the hook must state what is now possible that wasn't before.

rubrics_metrics.name: Real proof point (implicit quality rubric)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implicit requirement: include substantive proof—customer, data, or evidence supporting claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spokesperson quote that sounds human (implicit quality rubric)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implicit requirement: quotes should read like real human insight, avoiding boilerplate and taglines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embargo-then-wire distribution sequence (implicit quality rubric)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implicit expectation: follow embargo for exclusives, then broaden via wire and owned channels for SEO and reach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tied to measurable business outcome (implicit quality rubric)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implicit requirement: PR should be connected to measurable outcomes (hiring, leads, inbound, SEO) rather than vanity metrics.
